items.title: Pete Barbutti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 8, 2022
items.q: his piano player was Sarah Vaughan. I mean you know, and in those days everybody kept track of that in that generation. You know we knew all the sidemen in every band and everything.

ctx.x: Can I ask you, this is pretty specific, but if you were playing a gig down there and you played “Tutti Frutti” if you announced it as Pat Boone instead of Little Richard, would that have been okay?

I think so. Yeah. The difference didn’t seem so physical as it was metaphysical. Very strange. I still have a bad taste in my mouth from it. We also went to see — we were working a club in Shreveport, Louisiana and it was called the Great American City the sign said as we pulled in. And I saw in the newspaper Billy Eckstine and his band were going to appear there. And those were the old days when Billy wasn’t a star yet, because he was just starting to make some noise in the business, had a couple of hit records…

there, we kept our uniforms on, because we didn’t know what the situation was, and we wore a saxophone strap. So we walked in there and it was an unbelievable band and like a half hour later I get this poke in my back and turned around and it was a redneck white cop, said, “What are you doing in here?” And they threw us out. And I stopped the police car, I mean, we had no idea you know how dangerous it was because we were kids, we were still in our teens. And I explained what happened. And the cops said, “Well…
